title: Erdős Problem #137: powerful products of consecutive integers
abstract: Formalizes the abc-conditional finiteness results for Erdős Problem #137 (Erdős–Selfridge): a number N is powerful if every prime dividing N has its square dividing N, and the question is whether the product F(k,n) = n(n+1)⋯(n+k-1) of k ≥ 3 consecutive integers can be powerful for infinitely many n. Each route isolates its abc input (a radical lower bound) as a single explicit hypothesis and proves everything else outright, concluding that, conditionally, F(k,n) is powerful for only finitely many n for each fixed k ≥ 3.

informal.Erdos137.erdos137_finite: Under the Granville–Langevin radical bound RadLB k (an abc-conditional hypothesis) and k ≥ 3, the set of n ≥ 1 for which F(k,n) is powerful is finite.
informal.Erdos137.erdos137_eventually_not_powerfu: Under RadLB k and k ≥ 3, there is a threshold beyond which F(k,n) is never powerful.
informal.Erdos137.lemma_star: Unconditionally, the radical squared times the powerful part of m is at most m squared (rad m ^ 2 * B2 m ≤ m ^ 2).
informal.Erdos137.powerful_rad_sq_le: A nonzero powerful number N satisfies rad N ^ 2 ≤ N.
